# Part A: Pattern recognition (11:40-12:10)

## A1. The drill: four plots, four diagnoses

Run this chunk as-is. It simulates four datasets (I know the truth because the
code writes it), fits a straight line to each, and shows the four residual
plots.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
set.seed(2026)
n <- 100
x <- runif(n, 0, 10)
drill <- bind_rows(
  tibble(plot = "Plot 1", x = x, y = 5 + x - 0.2 * (x - 5)^2 + rnorm(n, sd = 1)),
  tibble(plot = "Plot 2", x = x, y = 5 + x + rnorm(n, sd = 1)),
  tibble(plot = "Plot 3", x = x, y = 5 + x + c(rnorm(n - 1, sd = 1), 8)),
  tibble(plot = "Plot 4", x = x, y = 5 + x + rnorm(n, sd = 0.22 * x))
)
drill_resid <- drill |>
  group_by(plot) |>
  mutate(fitted = fitted(lm(y ~ x)), resid = resid(lm(y ~ x))) |>
  ungroup()
ggplot(drill_resid, aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~plot, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Fitted values", y = "Residuals")
```

Match each plot to exactly one pathology from this list: **healthy (no visible
problem)**, **nonlinearity (curve)**, **nonconstant variance (fan)**, **single
outlier**. For each, one sentence on what visual feature gave it away.

- Plot 1: ...
- Plot 2: ...
- Plot 3: ...
- Plot 4: ...

call creates each pathology? ...

## A2. Now a real one: uninsured vs poverty

Fit the model and make the workhorse plot. (`lm()` drops counties with missing
values automatically; `poverty` is missing for many counties, so expect n
around 1,266.)

```{r}
#| eval: false
fit_pov <- lm(uninsured ~ poverty, data = county_health)

county_pov <- county_health |>
  drop_na(uninsured, poverty) |>
  mutate(fitted = fitted(fit_pov), resid = ___)

ggplot(county_pov, aes(x = ___, y = resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Fitted values", y = "Residuals")
```

**Which of the four drill patterns does this plot most resemble? Point to the
specific feature (where is the spread widest?).** ...

## A3. Residuals vs the predictor, plus the formal test

```{r}
#| eval: false
ggplot(county_pov, aes(x = ___, y = resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Poverty rate (%)", y = "Residuals")

car::ncvTest(fit_pov)
```

**Does the test agree with your eyes? In one sentence, why should the plot,
not the p-value, get the final word at n = 1,266?** ...
